claim: The census of handles. Up to isomorphism there are 24 non-planar knot spaces among the census's two (the Fano plane and census 58) and the splices of the Fano plane with the planar census spaces, both ways; minus each line they give 305 handles, each attached at a ladder in all six orders of its ports (1,830 cases, validated pipeline). (1) Every far halo line lies on the face opposite the port joined to the ladder's third line (the bottom port) or on the own arc of the other two ports; which faces are used depends only on the bottom port. Nine signatures occur (one entry per bottom port): no face 93, opposite at every port 75, both at every port 44, opposite at one port 33, opposite at one and both at two 33, own at two 10, opposite at every port and own at one 6, own at every port 6, own at one 5. Where the removed line sits largely decides it: lines inside a Fano atom read like the Fano plane, the intact Fano lines of a planar space spliced into the Fano plane read both faces at every port, glue lines mostly read nothing. (2) The claim rule of ticket A and its form in the handle's ports alone agree with the pipeline on all 3,660 (case, face) pairs: the opposite face of port c is used exactly when some removal and pair of handle points pin one class-c pattern while each point alone keeps both disagreeing values of the other two ports; the own arc of the other two is used exactly when a pair pins patterns of their classes with one of them fixed while each point alone keeps both class-c patterns. (3) The Fano plane (proved, with a finite check): every removal meets the removed line at one port a; pairs that pin one pattern pin a class-a pattern (336 of 336), and every single pin excludes exactly one pattern of each other class, on different values of those two ports, and at most one of class a (336 of 336). So it never uses an own arc (by the route direction of the claim rule) and uses the opposite face at every port (computed). (4) Census 58 uses the own arc exactly when the bottom port is 0 or 5, the third points of its two lines sharing the points 3 and 7 (48 of 48).
